original.target_description: Single fMRI study: bilateral amygdala BOLD activity, second-level analysis using overlapping extremity/fit voxels; interaction between scanning condition (positive versus negative) and stimulus valence (independent postscan positivity versus negativity ratings), F(1, 11).

n.sample_role: Participants retained for the within-participant fMRI analyses, including the target second-level interaction.
n.exclusions: Sixteen enrolled; two excluded for head motion greater than 2 mm in any direction, and two for knowing less than 75% of names. Unknown names were modeled separately; analyses used known names (91% on average).
n.location: Published article p. 153 (PDF page 2), Method, Participants; known-name restriction p. 154 (PDF page 3), Results.

es.location: Published article p. 156 (PDF page 5), Results, Separating Positive and Negative Aspects, interaction paragraph referring to Figure 3.

p.location: Published article p. 156 (PDF page 5), Results, Separating Positive and Negative Aspects, interaction paragraph referring to Figure 3.

replication.target_description: Unassigned replication side; not examined in original-only blind validation.

notes: Original-only fresh blind extraction. Supplied published article Affective Flexibility: Evaluative Processing Goals Shape Amygdala Activity, Cunningham, Van Bavel, and Johnsen (2008), rather than a manuscript/proof/supplement; title and authors verified on rendered PDF page 1. Locator p. 5 interpreted as PDF page 5 (printed page 156); the focal scanning-condition-by-stimulus-valence interaction linked to Figure 3 was selected. The input supplies no narrower outcome description; other regional tests also occur on this page. Rendered PDF page 5 confirms F(1, 11) = 9.67 and p < .01; rendered PDF page 2 confirms retained sample and exclusions. Canonical text renders the equals sign as digit 5 and the subscripted p-rep label as prep; exact quote glyphs retained, numerical meanings verified visually. No metric conversion. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not acquisition failures.
